text:
This looks like early 2013. Unemployment was 7.7% in February 2013, and the fed funds rate was about 0.12%. The 10-year yield was 1.87%, and VIX was 13.15 at the end of February 2013. US equities were up 11% over three months, consistent with a strong run from December 2012 through February 2013. Gold was down about 9.7% over six months, which also fits.

Headline CPI at 1.98% year over year matches January 2013 (1.6%) or February 2013 (2.0%). The latest CPI value is therefore February 2013, which was published in March, so the snapshot is probably end of February or March. The February 2013 unemployment rate of 7.7% was released in early March, and the S&P 500 returned about 1.4% in February. March 2013 was +3.8%, which matches the 1m return of +3.6%. The March 10-year yield was about 1.85%, also a match.

The unemployment rate in March 2013 was 7.6%, but it would not have been published until April. Because the 7.7% reading was the February figure, the snapshot is most likely end of March 2013, when the latest published CPI was still February's. Gold fell only 0.1% in March 2013, which fits.
